name: Tempester n°54: the beat roll follows the swing (option)
explanation: Tempester n°54: the beat roll follows the swing (Main 1.5.0.2). Docs/analyses/feature-roll-swing.md. Before: swing is applied only when an event's tick is computed ([routine]: step tick g with g % 48 >= 24 gets + s ticks, s = [address], 0-12). The beat roll ([address] = 1) repeats the window b0c / b10 (W ticks); [routine] projects each event to P = base + t % W in the current repetition, so every repetition is a copy of the source: a 1/16 roll on a straight step plays straight 16ths whatever the swing, and on a swung step every copy is late. After: while the roll is on and s != 0, a copy plays where the same note recorded at the copy's own step would play: copy nominal n (= its step tick), played at n + r + sw(n), r = Time Shift and half-step offset of the event, sw(n) = s if n % 48 >= 24 (the same rule, amount and grid as normal playback). In the repetition of the current tick x, a copy can only sit at P (window offset d = x - P = dA) or at the other swing phase (d = dB); RS_DECIDE tests the one that matches d and either keeps x (play) or returns a tick that is not x (skip). Swing 0, roll off or option Straight: P is left as it is, as before. Option (author, 12/11/2026: an on/off setting, default as before): System > Swing Source takes three more values, « Project+Roll », « Beat+Roll », « System+Roll »: the same swing source, and the roll swung. Stored as the source [address] / [address] (0-2, as before) plus [address] = 1, a byte of the System file that the stock OS saves and loads (halfword 109, file version > 6) and never uses otherwise (no instruction holds its address; default 0 from the defaults table [address], also on Reset System Parameters). An older OS reading the file ignores it. Edit: case 0x69 of [routine] jumps to RS_SRC_EDIT: [routine](source + 3 * roll, delta, 5), split back. Label: case 99 of [routine] (jump table word [address]) points to RS_SRC_LABEL: the stock label when roll = 0, otherwise the « +Roll » label of the source. Hooks: [address] (jal [routine](base, t % W)) goes through RS_STASH, which keeps t (the event tick of [routine]) in [address], then runs [routine] unchanged; [address] was jal [routine](P, 0x10) whose result nothing reads (pure arithmetic; next read of v0 is after another call): now RS_DECIDE, which may change s6 (P) before the note-off tick ([routine](s6, length)) and the comparison with x. Context: Timer 4 ([routine], only caller [routine]), so [address] is written and read by Timer 4 only. Leaf routines without stack; they write only v0, v1, a0-a3, t0-t9, hi/lo (all dead at the return: the caller reloads a0-a2 before its next call) and s6. No division: x % 24 parity by multiplication (0xAAAAAAAB, exact for every 32-bit value); s % W by subtraction (W = b10 != 0, tested, and at most 12 rounds since s <= 12).
